en: Midnight, Christians! it is the solemn hour,
When the God-man came down to us
To wipe away the original stain,
And to stop the wrath of his Father.
The whole world thrills with hope,
On this night that gives it a Saviour.
People, on your knees,
Await your deliverance,
Noël, Noël,
Here is the Redeemer,
Noël, Noël,
Here is the Redeemer.
May the burning light of our faith
Guide us all to the cradle of the child,
As once a shining star
Led there the chiefs of the East.
The King of kings is born in a humble manger;
Mighty ones of the day, proud of your greatness,
It is from there that a God preaches to your pride:
Bow, bow your brows before the Redeemer,
Bow your brows before the Redeemer.
The Redeemer has broken every shackle
The earth is free and heaven is open.
He sees a brother where there was only a slave:
Love unites those whom iron chained!
Who will tell him our gratitude?
It is for us all that he is born, that he suffers and dies:
People, stand up!
Sing your deliverance,
Noël, Noël,
Let us sing the Redeemer,
Noël, Noël,
Let us sing the Redeemer.
notes: line 1.3: 'la tache originelle', the original stain: original sin.
line 3.4: 'les chefs de l'Orient', the chiefs (leaders) of the East: the Magi.
line 3.6: 'Puissants du jour', the mighty of the present day.
'Noël' is kept as in the original: the Christmas cry.
